messages:
emma_support: customer reports CSV export for a large date range (90+ days) is incomplete. UI shows 2,450,000 rows but downloaded CSV stops early; last line is a partial row ending with \"...Refund for order 12345\" and no newline.

emma_support: repro steps i ran:
1) Console -> Analytics -> Export -> Custom range (2025-12-01 to 2026-02-28) -> CSV
2) Click download -> follow presigned URL
3) `curl -sSL \"https://redacted.s3.amazonaws.com/presigned/def...\" -o out.csv`
4) out.csv is 6,142,080 bytes but UI expected ~18,245,760 bytes

emma_support: `head -n3 out.csv` shows header + two rows. `tail -n1 out.csv` shows truncated last record ending mid-field.

emma_support: `curl -I` on presigned URL returns:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 18245760
Content-Type: text/csv
Accept-Ranges: bytes

raj_engineering: can you run `aws s3api head-object` against the object key referenced in the export job metadata? need to know the actual size on origin and Content-Encoding/Metadata.

emma_support: did that: `ContentLength: 18245760`, `ETag: \"deadbeef...\"`, `Metadata: {export-id: job_789}` — S3 shows full object.

olivia_pd: if origin contains full bytes but presigned download is truncated, likely the presigned proxy or our edge range logic is slicing incorrectly (maybe off-by-one when calculating the final range). could also be a connection abort.

raj_engineering: i'll tail proxy-service logs for requests matching that presigned token. also check proxy metrics around connection reset/timeout.

emma_support: found export-worker logs for job_789 (sanitized):
```
[export-worker] INFO export_id=job_789 streamed_rows=2450000
[export-worker] WARN export_id=job_789 multipart upload part 4 failed: write tcp 10.10.5.8:443->54.231.12.9:52112: write: connection reset by peer
[export-worker] INFO export_id=job_789 resumed upload part 4/8
[export-worker] INFO export_id=job_789 multipart upload completed
```

raj_engineering: worker shows retries but eventual completion. that aligns with S3 head-object showing full size. so the truncation must be occurring in the presigned/proxy path that serves the object to the client.

raj_engineering: can someone fetch the object directly from S3 via `aws s3 cp s3://redacted/exports/2026/job_789.csv ./from_s3.csv` from bastion and compare checksums against the client-downloaded file?

emma_support: did that: `sha256sum from_s3.csv = 3a1c...` and `sha256sum out.csv = 9f7d...` — mismatch confirmed.

raj_engineering: likely root cause: proxy-service uses range-based GETs to stream big objects to clients and calculates ranges using `Content-Length` as if it were the maximum byte index (should be total length). off-by-one or wrong subtraction could cause the last range request to be `bytes=0-18245759` vs `bytes=0-18245760` depending on logic, or worse, produce an empty final range when the chunk math results in negative length. if the proxy treats an empty response as EOF, client gets truncated.

olivia_pd: mitigation options: 1) flip per-org feature flag to use `buffered_exports` (upload whole file then generate presigned download of complete object) 2) ask infra to bypass proxy and give S3 direct presigned URL (if customer's S3 permissions allow) 3) re-run export with smaller chunk sizes.

infra-ops: i can toggle feature flag for org=org_789 to enable buffered_exports. doing it now.

infra-ops: feature flag enabled for org_789 (:white_check_mark:)

emma_support: asked customer to retry. they reported back after 8 minutes: full file downloaded and sha256 matches the s3 copy.

deploy-bot: [deploy] proxy-service/patch-258 scheduled canary deploy at 2026-03-17T15:20:00Z by raj_engineering :shipit:

raj_engineering: PR fix updates range math and adds unit tests around chunk boundary conditions (internal PR 258). also added instrumentation to emit `bytes_served_vs_origin` metric to detect discrepancies.

raj_engineering: follow-ups: add integration test for >2M row exports, add alert if >0.1% of downloads in a minute have mismatch between x-serve-bytes and origin size, and review connection pooling code paths that may close downstream sockets early.

emma_support: i'll update the customer ticket with the mitigation steps, timeline for canary, and note that we can re-run export or they can use the new buffered flow. closing thread unless canary shows problems. :thumbsup:

olivia_pd: excellent triage. please file incident and link to ticket.

emma_support: incident created: INC-2026-0456. linking to customer ticket now.
